title: English for Medicine and Health Care
overview: This practical English-language course equips healthcare professionals and support staff to communicate clearly, accurately, and empathetically in clinical and administrative settings. Through realistic healthcare scenarios, participants strengthen medical vocabulary, patient interviewing, explanations of care, professional handovers, written documentation, and communication across multidisciplinary teams. The program emphasizes language skills and communication practices rather than clinical diagnosis or treatment instruction.
audience: Doctors, nurses, allied health professionals, and clinical trainees seeking stronger workplace English.
Medical receptionists, patient coordinators, healthcare administrators, and customer service staff.
Pharmacists, laboratory personnel, and other healthcare employees who communicate with patients and colleagues.
Healthcare professionals preparing to work in English-speaking or multilingual care environments.
methodology: Interactive instruction combines targeted vocabulary development, guided listening and reading, patient–provider role-plays, simulated handovers, pronunciation practice, medical-document writing, case-based discussions, and constructive instructor feedback. Formative assessment includes short quizzes, communication checklists, and scenario-based speaking and writing tasks.
competencies: Confident, patient-centered spoken English and active listening in healthcare encounters.
Accurate use and pronunciation of common medical and healthcare terminology.
Clear patient questioning, explanations, and comprehension checks.
Professional clinical teamwork, handover, and escalation communication.
Concise and appropriate healthcare documentation and correspondence.
Culturally sensitive, confidential, and empathetic communication.
objectives: Use essential medical vocabulary to describe body systems, symptoms, conditions, and routine care processes.
Conduct structured patient introductions, history-taking conversations, and appointment discussions in English.
Explain routine procedures, instructions, and next steps using understandable, nontechnical language.
Recognize and clarify patient concerns, including language barriers and misunderstandings.
Communicate patient information concisely during referrals, handovers, and team discussions.
Read and draft common workplace documents, messages, and factual patient notes appropriately.
Apply respectful, empathetic language in sensitive or challenging interactions.
Demonstrate improved accuracy, fluency, and confidence in simulated healthcare situations.
